title: The Cat at the Vet
lines: Meg has a cat. It is a fat cat.
The cat has a cut on his leg.
Dad gets the van. Meg gets the cat.
The cat is mad. The cat hid.
Meg got the cat. It is not fun.
The van runs. The cat yips a lot.
The vet is a big man. He pats the cat.
The vet can fix the cut. The cat naps!
Meg hugs the cat. The cat is not mad.
We can go, Dad. The van is hot.

questions.ask: Why did Meg take the cat to the vet?
questions.listenFor: The cat had a cut on his leg. It is in the second line. If they say "he was sick," ask them to find the word that tells us.

questions.ask: How do you know the cat did not want to go?
questions.listenFor: The cat was mad, the cat hid, and the cat yipped in the van. Any one of those is a good answer - it is evidence, not a guess.

questions.ask: Do you think the cat will be scared next time? Tell me why.
questions.listenFor: There is no right answer. You want a reason from the story - the vet patted him and fixed the cut, or the ride was no fun. Follow the reason, not the answer.
